questions.q: What can a multimeter not show?
options: A short during a continuity test
questions.explain: A multimeter averages; only an oscilloscope sees fast events.

questions.q: Why use AC coupling when measuring 5 V ripple?
options: To remove the DC and zoom in on the scale
So you don't fry the oscilloscope input
questions.explain: Without AC coupling, ripple of tens of mV is invisible against 5 V.

questions.q: How many bits are in a DShot frame?
questions.explain: 11 throttle bits + 1 telemetry bit + 4 CRC bits = 16.

questions.q: Why does a long probe ground wire ruin a ripple measurement?
options: It cuts the probe bandwidth to 1 MHz
It picks up noise like an antenna
questions.explain: The ground loop is an antenna; a ground spring removes the artifact.

questions.q: At what baud rate do you decode CRSF between the receiver and the FC?
questions.explain: CRSF runs at 420000 baud; MSP is usually 115200.

questions.q: What does a NACK on an I2C address in the analyzer mean?
options: The bus is overloaded and needs a higher speed
There is no device at that address
questions.explain: No acknowledge — the device didn't respond.

questions.q: What is mandatory for any measurement on ESCs and motors?
How do you find a short with a multimeter before the first power-up?
options: A continuity test of the power bus + to − with no power
Measure current in the 10 A jack with the battery connected
Measure the voltage on the motors
Check the frequency on the signal wire
questions.explain: Continuity test before applying power: a beep between + and − means a short circuit.
